definition: A tracking technique that identifies users by collecting unique characteristics of their browser and device configuration.
metaDescription: Learn what browser fingerprinting is, how it works, and how to protect yourself from this invisible tracking technique.
simpleExplanation: Every browser leaves unique footprints based on its settings, installed fonts, screen size, and plugins. Websites collect these details to identify you without cookies.
whyItMatters: Browser fingerprinting works even in incognito mode and is nearly impossible to block completely. It allows companies to track you without your consent.
technicalDetail: Fingerprinting collects: User-Agent string, screen resolution, installed plugins, timezone, language, canvas rendering output, WebGL capabilities, audio context properties, and hardware concurrency.

examples.explanation: Ad networks use fingerprinting to track you across websites and serve targeted ads, even if you've cleared your cookies.
Banks use fingerprinting to detect suspicious login attempts by comparing device fingerprints to your usual browser profile.
